summary: Concordia University study of how the text used to represent repository files affects file-level bug localization. Datasets: 150 Long Code Arena tasks (50 each Python, Java, Kotlin; half multi-file) and 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Representations: file paths, raw source, and three GPT-OSS-20B summaries (role-aware, detailed technical, synthetic bug reports). These are tested under BM25, four small embedding models and Qwen2.5-Coder 7B/14B/32B as retrievers, plus reciprocal-rank fusion and Qwen 32B re-ranking of a top-20 list. No representation dominates. Role-aware summaries are 10-21x smaller than raw source and often competitive. Synthetic bug-report summaries hurt first-stage retrieval. LLM re-ranking adds the largest gains. An Agentless file-localization variant improves from 0.898 to 0.940 Hit@6.

claims.claim: Role-aware summaries outperform file paths by up to 40% Hit@5 while being 10.4-20.9x smaller than raw source
claims.evidence: Table 2: role summaries beat paths in 9 of 10 retriever-dataset cells (+21% to +55%; tie for Qwen3 on SWE). Footprint 9.9 vs 102.9 MTok (LCA) and 39.7 vs 830 (SWE). Raw source still beats role summaries in 4 of 5 SWE cells (BM25 .676 vs .440; Qwen3 .768 vs .626). As LLM retrievers, role summaries are below plain paths for Qwen 14B on both datasets (Table 5). Single run.

claims.claim: Combining representations improves Hit@5 by up to 31.9%
claims.evidence: Table 3: the 31.9% is one cell (GTE-Large, raw+paths, SWE). Many fused cells are negative (BM25 on SWE -18.9%; most dense 'lighter' pairs in Table 4). Fusion helps more consistently for LLM retrievers (Table 6).

claims.claim: LLM post-retrieval ranking improves Hit@5 by up to 42.0%
claims.evidence: Table 7: +17% to +49% over NORANK for paths, role summaries and bug-report summaries. NORANK is the file-path embedding first stage, the weakest retrieval setting. Ranking with paths alone gives nearly the same gains as ranking with role summaries (e.g. +39.4% vs +42.0%; +49.3% vs +37.0%). Raw-source ranking loses on SWE (-5.4%, -2.3%) because only 1-5 raw files fit in a 16K prompt for most instances.

claims.claim: In Agentless, role summaries plus ranking reach 94% Hit@6 (+4.7%)
claims.evidence: Table 8: 0.898 baseline, 0.918 with role summaries, 0.940 with ranking on SWE-bench Verified (about 10 and 21 more tasks out of 500). The baseline was re-run with Qwen2.5-Coder 32B. Single run; the extra ranking calls are not costed.

claims.claim: Summary generation is a cheap one-time cost (about $1.5-1.8 per repository)
claims.evidence: §7.2: $1,007 total for all three summary types over 650 repos at Groq GPT-OSS-20B rates. Regeneration after code changes is excluded from the cost.

patterns.note: Treats localization as the exploration step. The best representation flips with model size (summaries hurt Qwen 14B, help Qwen 32B) and with dataset. LLM retrievers often return a single file (309 of 500 on SWE). The pipeline is not agentic, so this informs what an exploration agent should index and see rather than testing an agent.

Role summaries as a compact file representation vs raw source: much smaller, and they fit a whole top-20 candidate list in a 16K ranking prompt. But raw source wins for BM25 and Qwen3 on SWE and makes the most unique localizations (Figs. 7-8). Detailed summaries are about 6x larger with no consistent gain.

BM25 over raw source is a strong, cheap first stage. It indexes the 1M-line Trino Java repo in seconds and beats every dense model on LCA raw source (0.627 Hit@5), but loses to 3 of 4 dense models on SWE raw source.
Dense embeddings beat BM25 on paths and summaries but not consistently on raw source, and embedding raw source takes up to 27 minutes for one large repo vs under a minute for BM25 (Table 9).

The closest analogue here is a generated per-file 'role and responsibilities' card rather than a domain glossary. It helps relative to paths with most retrievers and with Qwen 32B, but hurts with Qwen 14B, so its value depends on the reader model.

methodology.sample: LCA bug-localization test set: 150 tasks (50 Python, 50 Java, 50 Kotlin; 50% multi-file). SWE-bench Verified: 500 tasks (Python; 14% multi-file)
methodology.baselines: File-path representation; NORANK (embedding top-20 on paths); Agentless file localization re-run with Qwen2.5-Coder 32B
methodology.models: Summaries: GPT-OSS-20B via Groq. Retrievers: BM25 (Pyserini), GTE-Large, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, CodeXEmbed-0.4B, BGE-Large. LLMs: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B/14B/32B (16K context, temperature 0). text-embedding-3-small inside Agentless
methodology.variance: Single run per configuration (acknowledged); no confidence intervals
methodology.ablations: Full representation x retriever grid, fusion pairs, ranking representations; detailed summaries dropped from the LLM experiments for cost
methodology.contamination_controls: None; pretraining overlap with LCA and SWE-bench projects acknowledged and treated as an upper bound
methodology.languages: Python, Java, Kotlin (LCA); Python (SWE). No per-language breakdown is reported.

standards.peer_review: None stated (journal-formatted preprint with 'Received/Accepted: date' placeholders)
standards.artifacts: Code, prompts, generated summaries and databases, and all model outputs released (github.com/gencau/code-representations; Hugging Face)

biases.detail: Single runs across a large grid; small deltas cannot be separated from noise.
The abstract's headline gains (40%, 31.9%, 42.0%) are maxima over large grids in which many cells are flat or negative.
Ranking gains are measured against file-path embedding retrieval, the weakest first stage, and paths alone capture most of the re-ranking benefit.
Hit@5 credits a task when any one gold file is found, although half of LCA tasks need several files. LLM retrievers that return a single file can score well.
Public SWE-bench and LCA projects are likely in Qwen2.5 and GPT-OSS pretraining data.
SWE is Python-only and LCA results are not split by language, so Java behaviour cannot be read off.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None; open models and a commercial embedding inside Agentless
coi.detail: Academic study with no product at stake.

verdict_reason: A careful, fully released grid study across three languages with cost reporting. Against that: single runs; headline 'up to' numbers that are maxima over grids with many negative cells; a weak NORANK baseline for the ranking gains; Hit@5 crediting one of several gold files; and no per-language split, so Java cannot be isolated. The robust message is narrow: no single representation wins, and compact per-file role summaries are a cheap complement to raw-source lexical search, not a replacement.
applicability: For an exploration and onboarding agent over 4+ the repositories, this supports a cheap, deterministic design. Keep BM25 or grep over raw source as the first stage, since it is fast even on a ~1M-line Java repo. Add a cached or committed per-file role summary (what the class or module is responsible for) that agents and new developers can scan. Use an LLM to re-rank a candidate list shown as paths plus role summaries: 20 candidates fit in a 16K prompt, versus 1-5 raw files. Do not generate synthetic bug-report summaries for retrieval, and skip detailed technical summaries, which cost 6x the tokens for no consistent gain. Summaries hurt the 14B model, so a team using smaller or cheaper models must measure on its own repos. Regenerating summaries on change is not costed, so the team needs a staleness rule (for example, regenerate in CI when a file changes). Results are file-level within one repo and say nothing about cross-repo contracts.
